title: Calendar Observatory — curated international public dates
coverageDefinition: Named research cohort: 19 conventional G20 sovereign countries plus EU/African Union institutional targets, with additional inspected jurisdictions. Membership reference requests were unavailable/unreadable; no contemporary membership change was independently certified.
method: Bounded official-source requests through the inherited proxy with normal TLS verification. Date-relevant HTML, one PDF and public embedded calendar JSON were inspected by AI source readers. Short excerpts and hashes retained; no candidate profiling or election-outcome model.

sources.title: 2026 Congressional Primary Dates and Candidate Filing Deadlines for Ballot Access
sources.excerpt: General Election Date 11/03/2026
sources.support: Header explicitly states the national congressional general election date. Louisiana House runoff row lists 12/12 under RUNOFF DATE (IF NECESSARY).
limitations: The document states Dates Subject to Change and Data as of 5/18/2026. Retrieval on 29 October is not a new state-by-state confirmation.
This is a federal congressional schedule, not a complete calendar of state/local elections or polling-place opening times.

sources.title: CEC official Chinese homepage — serialized election calendar
sources.excerpt: "20261128","115年地方公職人員選舉投票"
sources.translation: Voting for the year-115 local public-office elections (ROC year 115 is 2026). The explicit serialized date is 20261128.
sources.support: The public homepage HTML includes a calendarList containing calendarId 56, date 20261128 and the local-election title. Values were decoded with JSON parsing and indexed references, without executing site code or making extra API calls.
limitations: The visible homepage shows only a nearby-week calendar; the future date was read from the official serialized calendar state.
Native Chinese title translated/paraphrased by an AI agent, not a certified translator.
This is local public-office voting across jurisdictions, not a presidential election, and does not define a single event instant.

Lima is only an illustrative study observer; it does not represent every affected centre.

events.title: Bulgaria presidential and vice-presidential election — second round
events.summary: Official CEC decision identifies the presidential and vice-presidential second round. The inspected date-relevant text was translated by an AI reader.
notes: Source confirms second round; first-round 25 October is past relative to 29 October.
Any noon sample is chosen for study and is not an election timestamp.

events.title: Peru populated-centre local authority elections
events.summary: ONPE’s dated release names voting in populated centres. This local process is distinct from a regional-governor runoff.
notes: ONPE 28 October release states 1 November voting in 2,262 populated centres.
These elections are organized by provincial municipalities with ONPE technical assistance; they are not the regional governor runoff.

events.title: World Philosophy Day
events.summary: Date calculated from UNESCO’s explicit third-Thursday rule. Its body also names a 19 November 2026 event; the page heading says 20 November and is retained as a source conflict.
notes: The page heading reads 20 November, while the explicit third-Thursday annual rule and a dated 19 November 2026 programme in the body agree. Use the cited rule-derived date; do not copy the heading as a fixed annual date.

events.title: United States congressional general election
events.summary: The FEC lists the congressional general election date. Its table is dated 18 May 2026 and explicitly says dates are subject to change.
notes: FEC source data dated 18 May; dates subject to change notice retained.
This national date spans multiple time zones and does not define one event instant.

events.title: World Science Day for Peace and Development
events.summary: An annual UNESCO observance of science in society. No particular local event clock or 2026 programme is inferred.

events.title: World Diabetes Day

events.title: International Day for Tolerance
events.summary: An annual international observance named by UNESCO’s account of UN General Assembly resolution 51/95.

events.title: International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women
events.summary: The annual date is supported by UNESCO’s source account. Individual programmes and their clocks vary.

events.title: 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence
events.summary: UN Women’s official 2026 campaign runs from 25 November through 10 December. The date range is inclusive; it does not imply one worldwide activity or event clock.
notes: This campaign range overlaps two annual international days; the entries are different public-date records, not independent astrological confirmations.

events.title: Victoria state election, Australia
events.summary: The Victorian Electoral Commission lists the state election date. This is a Victoria state event, not an Australian federal election.
notes: A regional/state election, not a federal election.
Noon sample is not the official start; opening hours are retained only in the source receipt.

events.title: Taiwan local public-office elections

notes: Date decoded from the official homepage public calendarList record, calendarId 56.

events.title: Louisiana United States House runoff — if necessary
events.summary: The FEC table lists this runoff date only if necessary. Whether any runoff will occur is not established by this snapshot.
events.condition: Only if a House runoff is necessary under the applicable election rules; occurrence has not been established.

This is not confirmation that a runoff will take place in every or any district.

coverage.note: A selected set of date rules from UNESCO, WHO, OHCHR and UN Women. Main UN pages returned access errors. This is not the full UN observance calendar or a list of every local activity.

limitations: Curated dates only: six confirmed election-date records, one optional conditional runoff, eight annual observance rules and one dated campaign range.
Annual projections start in 2026; no earlier historical observance coverage is implied.
Source availability and a fresh research timestamp do not guarantee that future schedules have not changed. Verify the issuing authority before operational use.
No date-only event is assigned an inferred capital, poll-opening, closing, result or global event timestamp.
No comprehensive country/holiday/festival/election coverage or astrological outcome validity is claimed.
